body: @yawkat sounds like a bug... looking into it now.
I _think_ delegating `channelInactive` and `handlerRemoved` to the decoder should fix it if that helps.
@yawkat yep something like that... working on it :)

I do think this change added a rather strange behavior to netty.

Assuming you have chain of:
- LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder
- MyCodec -> based on ByteToMessageCodec
- ...

In the past once the channel got closed, nothing happened. Which is somewhat expected.

With this change "MyCodec" gets it's `decode` method called with an empty buffer. Thus the initial idea of adding a `LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder` before the `ByteToMessageCodec` in order to ensure that only complete frames are passed on is irrelevant now, since `MyCodec` now always has to check for an empty buffer, or it will result in an `IndexOutOfBounds` exception.
Maybe a solution would be to only fire `decode` when there is actual data in the buffer.

Maybe we should only forward if it's not caused by a close of a Channel?

I am just digging through the source.

So `ByteToMessageDecoder` has `decodeLast` which is especially for this case. Defaulting to a call to `decode`. Same for the `ByteToMessageCodec`. So I would say, this is the same behavior now for both classes, which this issue is actually about.

However IMHO this is not what it should be in the first place looking at the idea in the javadoc of the `ByteToMessageDecoder`. However this may be just my point of view :wink: 

I guess I will open a new issue for this.

issue.title: ByteToMessageDecoder have to watch out for empty buffers

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Netty version: 4.0.31

Context:
Unexpected behavior when implementing a `ByteToMessageDecoder`. Following up in issue #4087.

The Javadoc of `ByteToMessageDecoder` urges the implementer to let another filter handle the actual frame detection, so that the implementation of `ByteToMessageDecoder` can focus on decode the content of the frame. Which is a good idea.

However will the `decode` method always be called when the channel is closed, even if there is no remaining data. This seems illogical (to me) since the prepended `LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder` has the task of not pushing through data in your chain which does not have a full frame (other decoders like `LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder`do the same).

So in the end implementations of `ByteToMessageDecoder` and `ByteToMessageDecoder` (since issue #4087 is fixed) do need to check for the received buffer size before being able to decode.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Implement a `ByteToMessageDecoder`
2. Add a `LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder` and your `ByteToMessageDecoder` implementation to the chain
3. Close the connection
4. `decode` gets called with an empty buffer
